trickyParts: The rebase GitHub's CONFLICTING forced: LEGION-15 removed flushEventLoopUntil, so the fifth daemon test now awaits the root stop arming its timeout sleep through a gate its own sleep fake resolves, and its one remaining tick-budget drain carries the required '// Negative wait:' line; the three console.error spies now restore in a finally, because a later test (LEGION-107's receipt_timeout) counts console.error calls and a spy left in place made it inherit this branch's three lines.

workspaceCommandRunner is a class field (the daemon runner with stderr normalised), shared by provisionWorkspace and removeWorkspace, typed as the workspace package's own run so both functions accept it unchanged.

removeIssueWorkspace asks jj only when <clone>/.jj exists, so a tree that closes without ever having provisioned logs nothing; every existing daemon close test under config('/state') therefore records no new command and no pin needed extending.

The fifth daemon test's 'after the close' instrument now reads the tree record at each jj command (every provisioning command must see `closed`): closeTree's returned promise spans the promotion sweep that follows the close, so a flag set on that promise no longer marks the close's end.

Both new fakes answer `split-window` (the re-admitted root's spawn splits into the tree's recorded window); without it the spawn fails, spawnRoot's catch re-queues the tree, and the retry close exercises a spawn-failure path instead of the scenario.
deviations: The plan expected 5 daemon tests to fail before the implementation; 4 did. 'runs no workspace removal at linger start' passes on today's code because beginLinger has never removed anything — it is a guard against moving the removal there, which the spec's acceptance 5 names explicitly, so it is kept.

The plan's test-file argv helpers (abandonCommand, forgetCommand, pruneCommand, ownCommitsCommand) were inlined into the one exact-pin expectation per the repository's tiny-functions rule; workspaceListCommand (three call sites) and gitWorktrees (asserts) stay.

reviewRound1.blocking: r4004189654 — closeTreeLocked(T) reached releaseSlot(T) → beginPromotionSweep → advancePromotionSweep → await startRoot(D) → spawnRoot(D) → awaitClosingTrees(D) while closingTrees still named T: D (a queued child of T with its own queued record) waited on the very close promoting it; neither settled. Reproduced by the reviewer (5 s timeout) and by the new regression against the previous processes.ts.
reviewRound1.fix: closeTreeLocked splices the slot out of admission.active without sweeping and returns whether it did (Promise<boolean>; closingTrees is Map<IssueKey, Promise<boolean>>); closeTree awaits the close (whose .finally deletes the map entry) and only then, when a slot was released, awaits beginPromotionSweep(). releaseSlot's other callers (beginLinger, recordRootExit, spawnTree's human-parked rollback) are unchanged. A StopFailed close releases no slot and sweeps nothing.
reviewRound1.foldIn: removeTreeWorkspaces keeps every workspace while state.admission.active includes the tree (reason `the tree holds an admission slot`), beside the not-lingering check: the StopFailed path rewrites the record lingering over a mid-close admit's active, so the sweep's retry close would otherwise remove the re-admitted root's fresh workspace. Spec version 4 records both decisions in Design.
